adds.title: Public Defender's Office of the State of Amazonas (DPE-AM) monitoring process, November 2023
adds.summary: As of 1 November 2023 the Amazonas Public Defender's health unit (Nudesa) had opened a collective preparatory procedure to enforce SUS access for trans people covering hormonization treatment, outpatient services and lack of authorization for transexualizing surgeries including sexual reassignment, and after an October 2023 meeting Manaus municipal health officials committed to dispense standardized medications on Ambulatório Codajás prescriptions for hormonization and to designate reference UBS primary-care units in each city zone while the state health secretariat was required to report on equitable care and hormoniotherapy gaps guaranteed under CFM Resolution 2.265/2019.

adds.title: Amazonas State Court of Justice (TJAM) booklet Home is a Right! / Lar e Direito!, August 2024
adds.summary: In August 2024 Amazonas established that LGBTQIAPN+ adolescents expelled from home are protected by ECA article 17 guaranteeing physical, psychic and moral integrity including identity, autonomy and beliefs, by constitutional and ECA duties of family, society and State to ensure health, food, education and protection from negligence and discrimination with equal treatment regardless of sexual orientation, by Law 14.811/2024 criminalizing bullying with penalties from fine to 4 years imprisonment, by the 2019 STF criminalization of homophobia as imprescriptible and non-bailable, and by the prohibition of gay-conversion therapy as illegal and ineffective, with legal support available through the Specialized Human Rights Public Defender's Office.

adds.title: Nationwide criminalization of homophobia and transphobia since 2019 / Amazonas protections since 2006
adds.summary: In Amazonas, Law 3079 since September 12, 2006 prohibits discrimination based on gender identity in all areas including employment and housing and since August 2, 2006 prohibits manufacture/sale/distribution of symbols inciting discrimination, prejudice, hatred or violence based on gender identity, since June 13, 2019 federal Supreme Court ruling criminalizes transphobia as a hate crime based on gender identity under Law 7,716/1989 with Maria da Penha domestic-violence protections extended to trans women in January 2022, since March 1, 2018 transgender people can change name and sex on birth certificate at a notary without surgery or medical letters, while non-binary recognition remains ambiguous case-by-case since April 18, 2022, bathroom access has no explicit protections, and since October 2, 2025 gender-affirming care is legal but puberty blockers and hormones are prohibited under age 18 and surgeries restricted to age 21+.

adds.title: State Law No. 6,463/2023 - gender-neutral language ban in schools, and STF suspension
adds.summary: Enacted 10 October 2023, Amazonas Ordinary Law No. 6463 expressly prohibits use of neutral language, non-binary dialect or any expression departing from standard Portuguese in curricula and teaching materials of public and private educational institutions and in official documents of educational institutions and public agencies throughout the state.

adds.title: Brazilian Public Security Forum / Brazilian Journal of Public Security data on anti-LGBTQ violence
adds.summary: In Amazonas in 2021-2022, crimes reported in the capital and interior involving homosexual, lesbian, bisexual and transsexual persons represented 0.36% of total reports, homophobia and transfobia motives and gender, sexuality, race and intersectionality categories were not identified in the records, LGBT victim data were few and poorly structured with victims not infrequently recorded as perpetrators due to failures in police occurrence reports, and public agents were unprepared to handle these demands.
